Persian zardozi is of three kinds: Some people completely sew the basic fabric with Bakhie (Persian: بخیه) in order to produce novel patterns and colors, such as the Baloch's Souzan-douzi (Persian: سوزن‌دوزی), Rasht's Qollab-douzi (Persian: قلاب‌دوزی) and Kerman's Pate-douzi (Persian: پَته‌دوزی).

Zardozi.question: It prospered during the 17th century during the reign of the _____ empire, but later a loss of royal patronage and industrialization led to its decline
Zardozi.fact: It prospered during the 17th century during the reign of the Mughal empire, but later a loss of royal patronage and industrialization led to its decline. Zardozi and chikan were historically favored by Mughal elites; products made in these styles symbolized wealth, power and status.
